children: Australian property developer Ingenia Communities Group
on Monday granted Warburg Pincus initial due diligence access on a non-exclusive basis after the US private equity firm raised its takeover offer for a third time.

The latest proposal, announced last week, values Ingenia at about A$2.14 billion ($1.49 billion). The A$5.25-a-share offer is nearly 4% higher than Warburg Pincus' previous A$5.05 offer, which Ingenia rejected as substantially undervaluing the company.
The due diligence access will allow Warburg Pincus to develop its revised indicative proposal into an offer.
In late August, Ingenia reached a A$992.5 million deal to buy residential property developer Peet
. Ingenia said on Monday it would not halt that effort despite Warburg's offer condition that Ingenia not pursue Peet.
Ingenia's board is assessing which deal would be better for shareholders and whether the Warburg proposal would qualify as superior as defined in the terms of the Peet agreement.
Shares of Ingenia Communities were up 1.9% at A$4.870 in early trade.
